title: Video making
summary: The fourth making card, beside Pictures, voice and song: which local video engine this machine reaches, whether the GGUF loader and the weight files are on disk, and the last clip it really wrote.

surfaces.usb: DEGRADED(a stick reaches no video engine until one travels with it, and the weights are ~18 GB - the card reports exactly that rather than reading empty)
surfaces.web: N/A(by the same steward decision as the other making cards: a browser tab has no local engine, no local weights and no output folder to report on, so a card there could only be decoration)

notes: Read-out (family 'info'), the fourth of the making cards. Every fact is asked of its OWNER - video_harness.app_state() for the engine install, adapter_state() for the GGUF loader, weights_state() for every declared weight file by name and size, models() for the recipes and their limits, and probe() for the live card - and none of it is re-derived here, so this card cannot drift out of step with the limb that renders. WHAT IT WILL NOT DO: it never claims a clip was made when none was. The last-clip row reports a file that is proven present and non-empty, or it says 'no clip rendered yet on this kit' - which is a TRUE fact on a fresh kit and stays green, exactly as an empty vault does on the memory card. The three ways a video engine can be unusable are kept SEPARATE and named separately - the app missing, the GGUF loader not registered, a weight file absent - because collapsing them is how a missing weight reads as a missing engine. A weight file that is declared and absent is reported as absent with its name, never folded into a percentage that reads as fine. It owns no state, writes nothing and gates nothing: its own test scans this source for write calls.
